_comment: Expected values for golden-session.jsonl -- the SHARED expectation that
the python suite (ctxmonitor package tests/) and core/tests/session-metrics.test.ts
(brokkr) BOTH assert.
A definition changed in one language breaks that language's assertion here.
Do NOT re-derive this file from whatever the code prints today: decide which
language is right, fix BOTH, then restate the expectation.
PROVENANCE. Every number below was HAND-COMPUTED from the fixture first (the
fixture's token values were chosen to make them come out on clean, exactly
representable boundaries), and only then confirmed by running the python scorer.
Nothing here was copied out of a program's output and blessed after the fact.
The hand arithmetic, per view:
prefix_legacy_final (records 0..12) -- scoreable 1,3,9,10,12
0+12000+0=12000 (null input/cache_creation => 0) |
cache_ratio         = 48750/65000 = 3/4 = 0.75 exactly
final turn = index 12, claude-haiku-4-5-... => 200k tier; 25000 < 200000 so
the inference net does NOT fire; occupancy = 25000/200000 = 1/8 = 0.125
prefix_over_window (records 0..16) -- adds scoreable 15,16
final turn = index 16, claude-opus-4-1-... => detected 200k, but its
effective input 250000 EXCEEDS 200000, so the '>window => 1M' net fires:
whole_session (all 26 records) -- adds scoreable 18,19,21
cache_ratio         = 490000/560000 = 7/8 = 0.875 exactly
final turn = index 21, claude-opus-4-10-... => 1M (the digit boundary keeps
the 200k token 'opus-4-1' from matching 'opus-4-10'); 187500 < 1000000 so
the net does not fire; occupancy = 187500/1000000 = 3/16 = 0.1875
Records 23 (synthetic) and 24 (sidechain) come AFTER index 21 and are excluded, so
the whole-session final turn is still 21 -- that is deliberate, not an oversight.
occupancy_fraction / cache_ratio are exact at 4 decimal places, so python's
round(x, 4) raw values compare equal to these literals with no tolerance needed.
scoreable_indices are indices into the PARSED record list (the fixture's '#'
header lines are skipped fail-open by both loaders); scoreable_uuids restate the
same set index-independently.
effective_input_by_index covers EVERY record that carries a usage OBJECT -- the
sidechain (4, 14, 24) and synthetic (6, 23) ones included, which no view sums. It
pins the effective_input FORMULA independently of the scoreable predicate, so a
change to one cannot hide behind the other. Records 8 (usage: null) and the user
records carry no usage object and are absent from the map by construction.

prefix_legacy_final.why: mixed-model session whose FINAL scoreable turn is a legacy 200k model: the window must come from the final turn's model, not the earlier 1M-tier turns

prefix_over_window.why: the FINAL scoreable turn is a legacy 200k model carrying more than 200000 effective input -- the '>window => 1M' inference net must fire

whole_session.why: the whole fixture: the FINAL scoreable turn is the digit-boundary model claude-opus-4-10-... (1M), and the synthetic + sidechain records after it must not become the final turn

window_map_probe.why: the model->window map read directly (detect_window / detectWindow), independent of any transcript: the digit-boundary discrimination is the part that rotted before

_comment: RECORDED, NOT BLESSED, AND NOT CLAIMED EXHAUSTIVE. The two implementations do NOT
agree everywhere. Each divergence below is real and PRE-EXISTING; each was found by
review of the change that added this fixture, measured, and
then left unresolved ON PURPOSE: closing any of them means changing a production
module's semantics, which is a behaviour decision with its own blast radius, not a
test. This section is the KNOWN set as of that review -- treat a future finding as an
addition to it, not as a contradiction of it.
None of these can live in the views above: the two languages compute DIFFERENT
answers for them, so no SHARED expectation could exist. Instead each case carries
BOTH answers, and each suite asserts its OWN language's number. Neither number is
endorsed as correct -- what is enforced is that the divergence stays exactly this
shape. If either side moves, its assertion breaks and whoever is standing there is
made to look at this record rather than discover the split years later.
1. effective_input_coercion -- NON-CANONICAL TOKEN VALUES.
context_quality.py coerces with `int(x or 0)` under a
TypeError/ValueError/OverflowError net, so a numeric STRING parses, a BOOLEAN
becomes 0/1, and a NEGATIVE survives. session-metrics.ts's toTokenInt admits only
a finite number greater than zero, so strings, booleans and negatives all become
0. They agree on float truncation and on unparseable values. Exposure: these
values do not appear in a well-formed Anthropic usage block -- the python coercion
net exists because ONE malformed number used to take the whole context signal
offline -- so this is a tail risk, which is why it survived unnoticed.
2. reported_fraction_rounding -- THE REPORTED FRACTIONS, NOT THE DEFINITIONS.
Both lanes compute the same quotient; they REPORT it at different precision.
context_quality.py's raw diagnostic dicts round to 4 decimal places
(occupancy_signal's occupancy_fraction, cache_efficiency_signal's ratio), while
deriveOccupancy / deriveCacheEfficiency hand back the raw double. The scores
themselves are interpolated from the UNROUNDED value on the python side, so this
is a reporting difference, not a scoring one -- but the two lanes do publish
different numbers, and a small fill is where it shows: 1 token in a 1M window is
0.0 from python and 0.000001 from typescript.
The views above are deliberately built on fractions that are exact at 4 decimal
places, which is what lets ONE shared expectation serve both languages there. That
is a construction choice, not evidence that the rounding agrees.
3. scoreable_predicate_usage_shape -- A JSON ARRAY AS `usage`.
python's _usage keeps the value only when isinstance(u, dict), so an assistant
record with `usage: []` is NOT a scoreable turn. The TS predicate accepts any
non-null `typeof usage === 'object'`, and an array passes -- so the same record
becomes a scoreable ZERO-token turn, which can take over lastModel /
lastEffectiveInput and move the reported final model, window and occupancy.
Unlike (1) this IS expressible in standard JSON; it still cannot be a fixture
record, for the same reason as the rest -- the two languages disagree about it.
Exposure: neither the SDK nor the CLI transcript writer emits an array usage, so
this is defensive-path only. python is the stricter of the two and is the side the
TS module's header claims to mirror.
4. record_shape_is_sidechain_truthiness -- A TRUTHY, NON-BOOLEAN isSidechain.
python excludes on any TRUTHY isSidechain (`not r.get(...)`), so "yes" excludes.
The transcript->SDK adapter in the TS test treats only the literal `true` as
subagent-attributed (and the TS predicate's own defensive check likewise tests
`=== true`), so the same record stays a scoreable top-level turn. The case below
runs through the test's REAL adapter, so it measures the documented mapping
contract rather than a convenience rewrite of it.
Exposure: near nil for the SDK lane, which never sees isSidechain at all -- it
attributes subagent turns with subagent_type / parent_tool_use_id. It is a
transcript-shape difference, and it is recorded because it is REAL, not because
it is likely.
5. absent_model_window -- A MISSING, NULL, EMPTY-STRING OR NON-STRING message.model.
The turn is scoreable on BOTH sides; what differs is the window. python's
detect_window maps such a model to the 1M DEFAULT and reports an occupancy
against it. The TS resolveWindow deliberately
returns undefined instead (its gate #4: with no model there is no window that can
be truthfully claimed, so the UI omits every window-derived field rather than
publish a default-window guess), and deriveOccupancy therefore reports nothing.
All FOUR spellings -- key absent, null, empty string, non-string -- behave the
same way on each side; null, "" and a dict are recorded as cases, and absent is
identical to null on both (python's .get returns None, the TS `typeof model ===
'string'` check yields undefined).
THE NON-STRING SPELLING IS NEW HERE AND USED TO BE A CRASH, NOT A
DIVERGENCE. python's `(model or "").lower()` raised AttributeError on a TRUTHY
non-string; both hooks call the scorer under a bare `except`, so that exception
surfaced nowhere and silently took the entire context signal offline. python's
`_model` now normalizes a non-string to None -- the same value an absent key
yields -- which makes this side agree with the TS predicate, and leaves only the
window split the other cases already record. The remaining split is unchanged.
This is the one split where the TS side's behaviour is a DOCUMENTED, deliberate
choice rather than an oversight -- do not 'fix' it by making the TS side guess 1M
without revisiting that gate. It is recorded here because the two lanes still
publish different things for the same transcript.
6. no_scoreable_turn -- A SESSION WITH NO SCOREABLE ASSISTANT AT ALL.
Both sides agree there are zero scoreable turns, and both report NO cache ratio
(python's raw ratio is None, deriveCacheEfficiency returns undefined). Occupancy
is where they part: python's occupancy_signal short-circuits to a REPORTED
fraction of 0.0 against the 1M default window ('no assistant usage; treated as
near-empty', which feeds a healthy 98.0 signal score), while deriveOccupancy
returns undefined -- nothing to report. So an idle or just-started session reads
as 'measured, 0% full' from one lane and 'no measurement' from the other. Both
are defensible; they are not the same statement, and a consumer that treats
undefined as 0 (or 0 as measured) will get one of them wrong.
ONE FURTHER DIVERGENCE, prose-only because it genuinely cannot be written into this
file at all:
7. LOADER, NON-STANDARD JSON TOKENS. python's json.loads accepts the bare tokens
NaN / Infinity / -Infinity inside an object, so read_jsonl KEEPS such a record;
JSON.parse rejects the line outright, so the TS test's loader SKIPS it. The two
loaders therefore agree on this fixture and on ordinary malformed JSON, but not
on that non-standard form. Those tokens are not legal JSON, so no standard
writer can emit them into this file -- unlike the large-integer parser split,
which IS legal JSON and is recorded as a case under (1).

reported_fraction_rounding.why: python rounds the fraction it REPORTS in its raw diagnostic dicts to 4dp; the TS derive* functions return the raw double. Same quotient, different published number.

occupancy_cases.why: 1 token in a 1M window: python's 4dp rounding erases the fill entirely

cache_ratio_cases.why: 1/32 is exact in binary but needs 5 decimal places, so the 4dp rounding shows

scoreable_predicate_usage_shape.why: python's _usage requires isinstance(dict); the TS predicate accepts any non-null typeof 'object', so a JSON ARRAY passes and becomes a zero-token turn

record_shape_is_sidechain_truthiness.why: python excludes on ANY truthy isSidechain; the transcript->SDK adapter and the TS predicate both key on the literal true, so this stays a scoreable top-level turn

absent_model_window.why: scoreable on both sides; python defaults an absent model to the 1M window and reports occupancy against it, while the TS resolveWindow returns undefined by design (gate #4) so no window-derived field is published. An ABSENT model key behaves identically to this explicit null on both sides.
the EMPTY-STRING spelling of the same split: python's (model or '').lower() sends it to the 1M default, while resolveWindow's model.trim() === '' check returns undefined

the NON-STRING spelling. Until then this record was not a divergence at all -- it was a CRASH: python's detect_window did (model or '').lower(), and a truthy non-string sailed past the `or` and raised AttributeError, which both hooks swallowed under a bare except, silently taking the whole context signal offline. _model now normalizes a non-string to None, so this side behaves exactly like the null/empty-string cases above and the TS side (which has always ended with `typeof model === 'string' ? model : undefined`) is unchanged. What is left is the SAME window split as the other two cases, which is why it is recorded here rather than as a new divergence.

no_scoreable_turn.why: both sides agree on zero scoreable turns and on reporting NO cache ratio; only occupancy parts -- python short-circuits to a reported 0.0 against the 1M default ('treated as near-empty'), the TS side reports undefined (nothing measured)

effective_input_coercion.why: python keeps a negative (int(-1)); TS toTokenInt requires v > 0
python int() parses a numeric string; TS requires typeof v === 'number'
python int(True) == 1; TS requires typeof v === 'number'
the negative propagates into the SUM on the python side only
AGREE: both truncate a float toward zero
AGREE: an unparseable value is 0 in both (python's fail-open coercion net)

the split here is in the PARSER, not the coercion: 2^53+1 is legal JSON and survives python's json.loads exactly, while JSON.parse rounds it to the nearest double (2^53) before toTokenInt ever sees it. This case is self-demonstrating -- each side reads the SAME literal from this file and its own parser hands it a different number. Exposure is nil in practice (a real token count is ~1e6), but it is legal JSON, so it belongs here as a case and not in the prose.
